summary.description: Finds communities in the reviewed graph and keeps those that contain main people. Orders them by the main members’ birth years and identifies each circle by its main members.
summary.input: the reviewed graph
summary.output: ordered circles with members and ties

summary.description: Collects the names that link a meta story to its translated person stories. People are named as their localized registry entries name them; only map places are looked up in Wikipedia language links.
summary.input: the composed meta story and localized person data
summary.output: name evidence for people and places

summary.description: Selects the people who fit the theme from their roles, summaries, places, and events. Writes the story’s title, introduction, subtopics, chapters, and conclusion, and names people missing from the registry.
summary.input: the person registry and life events
summary.output: a story plan and selected people

summary.description: Filters the selected people’s life events to major contributions relevant to the theme and records why each kept event is relevant. Biographical and routine events are removed by default.
summary.input: the selected people and life events

summary.description: Adds to each chapter a few dated historical events that directly affected the people it follows. A chapter may receive none.
summary.input: the fitted chapters with their surviving events

summary.description: Combines the selected people’s ego networks into one social graph by matching names. It keeps direct ties, acquaintances shared by several main people, and each person’s account of a direct relationship.
summary.input: selected people and ego networks

summary.description: Reviews the merged network against the article evidence, adding missed direct ties and removing vague or indirect ones. Graph density sets how readily it proposes new ties.
summary.input: the merged network

summary.description: Writes a factual title and short text about the ties of each detected circle and stores the circle’s members with it.
summary.input: the circles to narrate
summary.output: a title and text per circle

summary.description: Groups rated events into places whose members all lie within a distance limit. Centers each place on its more important events, keeps the highest-scoring places, and orders them in time.
summary.input: located events and per-event weights
summary.output: selected map stops with their events

summary.description: Rates each located event by how relevant its place is to the story’s theme. The ratings weight the place clustering.
summary.input: the chapters and life events

summary.description: Writes a short factual title and text for each geographic cluster and discards the clusters that are not relevant to the story.
summary.input: the qualifying geographic clusters
summary.output: map stops with titles and texts

summary.description: Rewrites the circle, timeline, and map texts as one story in a consistent style, sets their order, and removes map stops that do not fit the story.
summary.input: circle narration, map stops, and background material

summary.description: Derives a dark color, type, pattern, and ornament system for the story from its framing and opening. The patterns are abstract geometry.
summary.input: the story’s framing and opening

summary.description: Translates the meta story, taking person names and event titles from the localized person data. Each recurring metaphor is translated the same way throughout.
summary.input: the meta story and localized person data

summary.description: Checks for each deep event whether the reviewed sources hold material about the event itself, and writes a background report only where they do. Sets each event’s citations from the articles it was given.
summary.input: the reviewed events and source articles

summary.description: Draws one abstract image for each chapter from its concept, in the portrait style and the story’s colors.
summary.input: chapter concepts, story colors, and style
summary.output: an illustration for each current chapter

summary.description: Develops an abstract visual concept for each chapter from the life events. All chapters are drafted together so their metaphors differ, and no concept depicts the person, a place, or a historical event.
summary.input: the finished life events
summary.output: an abstract visual concept per chapter

summary.description: Selects the most significant events of the life, weighs them against each other, and groups them into chapters. Leaves dated event skeletons and a conclusion about the person’s lasting work.
summary.input: the article and selected related articles
summary.output: a chaptered life timeline and conclusion

summary.description: Researches each proposed event against the subject’s article and event-specific related articles. It expands the event into prose, places, people, sources, annotations, an icon, and image search terms.
summary.input: an event skeleton and Wikipedia material

summary.description: Adds map coordinates to the places in the life events, geocoding each place by its modern name where the research supplied one.
summary.input: historic and modern place names

summary.description: Decides the target-language form of each person name before translation and writes one glossary shared by the life events, network, and registry. Source evidence takes priority where it identifies the same person.
summary.input: name evidence and person names

summary.description: Checks Commons results against each report and keeps only pictures that directly depict things the report names. It reads filenames together with captions, and code admits one result per search.
summary.input: the report, its searches, and life events

summary.description: Runs the planned searches and each event’s own searches against Commons and Openverse and keeps one candidate per picture URL. The event searches run first, so a picture keeps the event it was found for.
summary.input: the planned and event image searches
summary.output: deduplicated image candidates linked to events

summary.description: Scores every image hit on resolution, file efficiency, filename, and commemoration, drops those below a threshold, and ranks the rest. Plaques and graves receive a penalty.
summary.input: every image hit the queries returned

summary.description: Picks a reference portrait and assigns an image to a life event only where the image depicts the event directly. An event without such an image stays unillustrated.
summary.input: the ranked image candidates

summary.description: Plans Commons searches for the life: a few for the person, from which the portrait is chosen, and the rest for things the events name. It excludes commemorative objects such as plaques and statues.
summary.input: the event skeletons

summary.description: Checks the chosen portrait against the person in the story by inspecting the image itself. It removes a rejected portrait before the life events and person registry are written.
summary.input: the portrait pick

summary.description: Fetches the person’s article in the target language and the target-language names linked to the people and places in the data. A comma-qualified place without a link is looked up again under its leading name.
summary.input: reviewed names, life events, and ego network

summary.description: Builds the subject’s network of documented direct ties to named people from the finished life events and Wikipedia material. Institutions are not included as people.
summary.input: finished life events and Wikipedia material
summary.output: a documented network of personal ties

summary.description: Redraws the person’s licensed reference portrait in the shared drawing style and the story’s colors, keeping the likeness, and records the finished portrait with the person’s data.
summary.input: the person registry and interface style
summary.output: a portrait and updated person registry

summary.description: Reviews the life events and ego network together against the source articles and proposes corrections and prose revisions. Only changes the critic rates with high confidence are applied.
summary.input: the life events, network, and source articles
summary.output: reviewed life events and ego network

summary.description: Derives a dark color, type, and pattern system from the person’s work, places, and pictured objects, and names the sources of the palette. Rejects styles with insufficient contrast or without a named source.
summary.input: the finished life events and image captions
summary.output: a palette, type system, and pattern

summary.description: Translates the narrative text of the person’s events, network, registry entry, and reports, applying the name glossary and target-language evidence. The merge keeps dates, coordinates, links, and identifiers from the English record.
summary.input: the person record, reports, and name mapping

summary.description: Fetches the subject article, candidate related articles, and Commons image metadata, and caches them under the subject’s identifier for the later steps.
summary.input: a subject or article URL

summary.description: Ranks the linked articles by relevance to the life story and keeps those about people, personal events, and individual works.
summary.input: the article and outgoing link candidates
